text: {"covered": true, "see_a_professional": false, "sentences": [{"sources": [1], "text": "Early signs of vitamin B12 deficiency often include typical anemia symptoms like fatigue, paleness, shortness of breath, headaches, or dizziness."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "If the condition is not treated, you may experience brain and nervous system issues such as tingling, pain, trouble walking, or uncontrollable muscle movements."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "Other potential symptoms include confusion, memory loss, mood changes like depression, and problems with smell, taste, or vision."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "Physical signs can also involve diarrhea, weight loss, and glossitis, which is a painful, smooth, red tongue."}, {"sources": [2], "text": "Untreated vitamin B12 deficiency can lead to serious complications, including bleeding, infections, and permanent damage to the brain or nerves."}, {"sources": [5], "text": "Some symptoms, particularly those affecting the brain or nerves like numbness and tingling, may not fully resolve even after treatment."}]}

{"covered": true, "see_a_professional": false, "sentences": [{"sources": [2], "text": "Your body cannot produce vitamin B12 on its own, so you must obtain it from food or supplements."}, {"sources": [3], "text": "The primary natural sources of vitamin B12 are animal products such as lean red meat, chicken, fish, seafood, eggs, and dairy items."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "Following a strict vegan diet means avoiding these animal-based foods, which can lead to insufficient intake of the vitamin."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "While this risk exists, vitamin B12 deficiency is actually rare in the United States compared to other causes like absorption issues."}, {"sources": [3], "text": "Vegans can prevent deficiency by consuming fortified foods like certain cereals, vegan milk substitutes, or by taking supplements."}, {"sources": [2], "text": "Without enough vitamin B12, the body cannot properly form healthy red blood cells, leading to a condition known as anemia."}]}

{"covered": false, "see_a_professional": false, "sentences": [{"sources": [1], "text": "The provided sources do not state the specific daily amount of vitamin B12 required for pregnant women."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "They note that recommended daily amounts depend on age, sex, and pregnancy status, and that a healthcare provider can help determine your specific needs."}, {"sources": [2, 5], "text": "The sources do cover other specific nutrient needs during pregnancy, such as 27 mg of iron, 1,000 mg of calcium, 600 IU of vitamin D, and 600 mcg of folic acid per day."}]}

{"covered": true, "see_a_professional": false, "sentences": [{"sources": [1, 3, 5], "text": "Good sources of iron include beans, dried fruits, eggs, lean red meat, salmon, iron-fortified breads and cereals, peas, tofu, and dark green leafy vegetables."}, {"sources": [3], "text": "Other high-iron foods include lean meat, seafood, poultry, white beans, lentils, spinach, kidney beans, nuts, and raisins."}, {"sources": [1, 5], "text": "Vitamin C-rich foods such as oranges, strawberries, and tomatoes help your body absorb iron."}, {"sources": [5], "text": "Some foods like black tea can reduce iron absorption."}, {"sources": [3], "text": "Iron is found naturally in many foods and is also added to some fortified food products."}, {"sources": [3], "text": "The amount of iron you need each day depends on your age, sex, and whether you consume a mostly plant-based diet."}, {"sources": [3], "text": "People who are pregnant or breastfeeding are more likely to have low iron levels."}]}

{"covered": true, "see_a_professional": true, "sentences": [{"sources": [1], "text": "Iron supplements, also known as oral iron, are the most common treatment for iron-deficiency anemia."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "It often takes three to six months to restore iron levels with these supplements."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "Intravenous iron is sometimes used to increase blood iron levels, particularly for people with serious anemia or long-term conditions."}, {"sources": [2], "text": "Medicines called erythropoiesis stimulating agents may be used with iron therapy if bone marrow issues are causing the deficiency."}, {"sources": [2], "text": "Blood transfusions can quickly increase red blood cells and iron in cases of serious anemia."}, {"sources": [2], "text": "Surgery may be required to stop internal bleeding that is causing the anemia."}, {"sources": [2], "text": "Doctors may also recommend eating iron-rich foods like beans, lean red meat, and dark green leafy vegetables."}, {"sources": [2], "text": "Consuming foods rich in vitamin C can help your body absorb iron better."}, {"sources": [1, 2], "text": "A doctor or registered dietitian should advise you on the specific treatment plan and any dietary changes."}]}

{"covered": true, "see_a_professional": true, "sentences": [{"sources": [1, 2, 4], "text": "Heavy periods are a recognized cause of anemia because losing blood also means losing the iron your body needs to make hemoglobin."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "While some blood loss during the menstrual cycle is normal, anemia resulting from bleeding too much is not considered normal."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "You should see a doctor if you need to change your tampon or pad after less than two hours or if you pass clots the size of quarters or larger."}, {"sources": [2, 3], "text": "Anemia occurs when your blood does not carry enough oxygen to the rest of your body, which can make you feel tired, cold, dizzy, or short of breath."}, {"sources": [3], "text": "Women during their menstrual periods are at a higher risk for developing anemia."}, {"sources": [4], "text": "Blood loss from heavy menstrual periods is a specific factor that can lead to iron-deficiency anemia."}, {"sources": [2], "text": "A doctor can diagnose anemia through a physical exam and blood tests, and treatment depends on the specific type of anemia you have."}, {"sources": [], "text": "A doctor or registered dietitian should advise you on managing heavy periods and potential anemia."}]}

{"covered": true, "see_a_professional": false, "sentences": [{"sources": [1], "text": "Anemia is common during pregnancy because your body produces more blood to support your baby's growth."}, {"sources": [1, 4], "text": "This increase in blood volume means you need more iron and other nutrients for both yourself and your developing baby."}, {"sources": [2, 3], "text": "Iron is essential for making hemoglobin, the protein that carries oxygen from your lungs to the rest of your body."}, {"sources": [1, 2], "text": "If you do not get enough of these nutrients, your body may not produce enough healthy red blood cells, leading to anemia."}, {"sources": [1, 2], "text": "Women are at a higher risk for anemia during pregnancy compared to other times in their lives."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "Doctors typically recommend prenatal vitamins and may suggest additional supplements to help prevent this condition."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "Untreated anemia during pregnancy can lead to complications such as preterm labor and low birthweight."}]}

{"covered": true, "see_a_professional": false, "sentences": [{"sources": [1], "text": "Undiagnosed or untreated iron-deficiency anemia may cause serious complications such as fatigue, headaches, restless legs syndrome, heart problems, pregnancy complications, and developmental delays in children."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "Iron-deficiency anemia can also make other chronic conditions worse or cause their treatments to work poorly."}, {"sources": [5], "text": "If you have too little iron, you may develop iron-deficiency anemia."}, {"sources": [5], "text": "It may not cause symptoms at first, but over time, it can cause fatigue, shortness of breath, and trouble with memory and concentration."}]}

{"covered": true, "see_a_professional": false, "sentences": [{"sources": [2], "text": "Primary hemochromatosis is an inherited condition caused by gene mutations that affect how the body absorbs iron from food."}, {"sources": [2], "text": "Secondary hemochromatosis occurs when there is too much iron in the diet or from frequent blood transfusions."}, {"sources": [2, 4], "text": "Neonatal hemochromatosis is a rare condition where liver injury in a fetus leads to iron buildup in the liver and other organs."}, {"sources": [2], "text": "These different types result in an excess of iron stored in the body's tissues."}, {"sources": [3], "text": "Doctors typically treat the condition by drawing blood to lower iron levels."}, {"sources": [3], "text": "Treatment helps improve symptoms and prevents potential health complications."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "Diagnosis usually involves blood tests and a review of medical and family history."}]}

{"covered": true, "see_a_professional": false, "sentences": [{"sources": [3], "text": "Doctors may order blood tests to check levels of iron, transferrin, and ferritin."}, {"sources": [3], "text": "These tests also measure the ratio of iron to transferrin in the blood."}, {"sources": [3], "text": "A high ratio of iron to transferrin may suggest a person has hemochromatosis."}, {"sources": [3], "text": "High ferritin levels are also typical in people with hemochromatosis."}, {"sources": [3], "text": "Doctors use ferritin blood tests to see if iron levels are improving with treatment."}, {"sources": [3], "text": "Blood tests can also check for gene mutations that cause hemochromatosis."}, {"sources": [3], "text": "Finding two copies of the HFE gene with the C282Y mutation confirms the diagnosis of primary hemochromatosis."}]}

{"covered": true, "see_a_professional": false, "sentences": [{"sources": [3], "text": "Vitamin D deficiency means your body is not getting enough vitamin D to stay healthy."}, {"sources": [3], "text": "This vitamin helps your body absorb calcium, which is a main building block of bone, and supports your nervous, muscle, and immune systems."}, {"sources": [1, 3], "text": "Deficiency can occur if you do not get enough vitamin D from your diet, sunlight, or supplements, or if your body cannot absorb or convert it properly."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "Breastfed infants are at higher risk because human milk is a poor source of vitamin D."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "Older adults are at risk because their skin produces less vitamin D from sunlight and their kidneys are less able to convert it to its active form."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "People with dark skin are at higher risk because their skin has less ability to produce vitamin D from the sun."}, {"sources": [1, 2], "text": "Individuals with conditions that affect nutrient absorption, such as Crohn's disease, celiac disease, or obesity, are also at increased risk."}, {"sources": [2], "text": "People who have had gastric bypass surgery or have chronic kidney or liver disease are at higher risk for deficiency."}, {"sources": [2], "text": "Those taking certain medicines, including some cholesterol, anti-seizure, steroid, and weight-loss drugs, may also be at risk."}]}

{"covered": true, "see_a_professional": false, "sentences": [{"sources": [1], "text": "Severe vitamin D deficiency in children can cause a rare disease called rickets."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "Rickets causes the bones to become soft and bend."}, {"sources": [2], "text": "Vitamin D is necessary for the body to absorb calcium, which is a main building block of bone."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "African American infants and children are at a higher risk of developing rickets."}, {"sources": [3], "text": "Breastfed infants are at higher risk of vitamin D deficiency because human milk is a poor source of the vitamin."}, {"sources": [3], "text": "Health providers recommend giving breastfed infants a daily supplement of 400 IU of vitamin D."}, {"sources": [2], "text": "The recommended daily amount of vitamin D for children aged 1 to 13 years is 600 IU."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "A blood test can measure how much vitamin D is in your body."}]}

{"covered": true, "see_a_professional": false, "sentences": [{"sources": [1, 2], "text": "Vitamin K is one of the thirteen vitamins your body needs to grow and develop normally."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "It helps make proteins that are essential for healthy bones and tissues."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "Vitamin K also produces proteins required for blood clotting."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "If you do not have enough vitamin K, you may experience excessive bleeding."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "Most people obtain this vitamin from plants such as green vegetables and dark berries."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "Bacteria in your intestines also produce small amounts of another type of vitamin K."}, {"sources": [2], "text": "Your body can also make vitamin K naturally."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "Newborns have very little vitamin K and usually receive a shot of it soon after birth."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "People who take blood thinners need to be careful about how much vitamin K they consume."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "Vitamin E supplements can interfere with how vitamin K works in your body."}]}

{"covered": true, "see_a_professional": false, "sentences": [{"sources": [1, 2], "text": "Folic acid is a B vitamin that helps the body make healthy new cells."}, {"sources": [2], "text": "Getting enough folic acid before and during pregnancy can prevent major birth defects of the baby's brain or spine."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "These specific birth defects are known as neural tube defects."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "Women need 400 micrograms of folic acid per day before pregnancy."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "During pregnancy and breastfeeding, the recommended amount increases to 600 micrograms per day."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "It is difficult to get this amount from food alone, so a supplement is usually needed."}, {"sources": [2, 5], "text": "Pregnant women can take folic acid supplements to help prevent certain birth defects."}]}

{"covered": true, "see_a_professional": false, "sentences": [{"sources": [1], "text": "Vitamin A is a nutrient that your body requires for normal growth and development."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "It plays a key role in maintaining vision, supporting bone growth, and aiding reproduction."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "Vitamin A also supports cell functions and helps maintain a healthy immune system."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "As an antioxidant, it can be obtained from plant sources like colorful fruits and vegetables or animal sources such as liver and whole milk."}, {"sources": [4], "text": "Getting enough vitamin A helps prevent specific health issues, such as night blindness."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "Certain groups, including vegetarians, young children, and individuals with conditions like liver disease or cystic fibrosis, may need extra vitamin A."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "You should consult a health care provider to determine if you need to take vitamin A supplements."}]}

{"covered": true, "see_a_professional": false, "sentences": [{"sources": [1], "text": "Adults aged 19 to 50 need 1,000 milligrams of calcium daily."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "Men aged 51 to 70 also need 1,000 milligrams per day."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "Women aged 51 to 70 and adults 71 and older need 1,200 milligrams daily."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "Pregnant and breastfeeding adults require 1,000 milligrams of calcium each day."}, {"sources": [2], "text": "You can obtain calcium from foods and supplements."}, {"sources": [2], "text": "Dairy products like milk, cheese, and yogurt are the main food sources for most people in the United States."}, {"sources": [5], "text": "Other food sources include leafy green vegetables, fish with soft bones, and calcium-enriched foods."}, {"sources": [5], "text": "Calcium is also available in supplements and many multivitamins."}]}

{"covered": true, "see_a_professional": false, "sentences": [{"sources": [3], "text": "Osteoporosis is a disease where bones become weak and are likely to fracture because bone mass decreases or bone structure changes."}, {"sources": [3], "text": "It is often called a silent disease because it usually does not cause symptoms until a bone breaks."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "A diet low in calcium, vitamin D, or protein can raise your risk of developing osteoporosis."}, {"sources": [2], "text": "Eating a healthy, balanced diet that includes enough calcium, vitamin D, and protein is recommended to help manage the condition."}, {"sources": [2], "text": "To help prevent osteoporosis and keep bones strong, it is best to eat a diet rich in calcium and vitamin D."}, {"sources": [5], "text": "Vitamin D deficiency can lead to a loss of bone density, which contributes to osteoporosis and fractures."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "Other lifestyle factors like smoking, heavy alcohol use, and physical inactivity also contribute to bone loss."}, {"sources": [2], "text": "Regular physical activity, including weight-bearing exercise, helps support bone health alongside dietary changes."}]}

{"covered": true, "see_a_professional": false, "sentences": [{"sources": [1, 5], "text": "Your body needs some sodium to help nerves and muscles function and to maintain the right balance of fluids."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "If you consume too much sodium and your kidneys cannot remove the excess, it builds up in your blood."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "This buildup can lead to high blood pressure, which can cause other health problems."}, {"sources": [1, 4], "text": "The Dietary Guidelines recommend that most adults limit their sodium intake to less than 2,300 milligrams per day."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "This amount is equivalent to about one teaspoon of table salt per day."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "People with high blood pressure, diabetes, or kidney problems, as well as African Americans and those over age 50, are more sensitive to salt and should eat less."}, {"sources": [3], "text": "Eating a diet rich in potassium can help offset some of the harmful effects of sodium on blood pressure."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "Reading food labels can help you identify and limit the amount of sodium in prepared foods."}]}

{"covered": true, "see_a_professional": false, "sentences": [{"sources": [1, 2, 5], "text": "Potassium is a mineral and electrolyte that is essential for your body to function properly."}, {"sources": [1, 2, 5], "text": "It helps your nerves function and allows your muscles to contract."}, {"sources": [1, 5], "text": "Potassium works to keep your heartbeat regular and steady."}, {"sources": [1, 5], "text": "It assists in moving nutrients into your cells and waste products out of them."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "Eating a diet rich in potassium can help offset some of the harmful effects of sodium on blood pressure."}, {"sources": [3], "text": "As a macromineral, potassium is one of the minerals your body needs in larger amounts to stay healthy."}, {"sources": [5], "text": "Electrolytes like potassium also help balance the amount of water in your body and maintain acid-base levels."}]}

{"covered": true, "see_a_professional": false, "sentences": [{"sources": [1], "text": "Malnutrition means that your body isn't getting enough calories or the right balance of nutrients to stay healthy."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "This condition can result from not getting enough protein, carbohydrates, and fats, eating too much unhealthy food, or lacking necessary vitamins and minerals."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "While often associated with undernutrition, malnutrition can also refer to overnutrition or an imbalance of nutrients."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "Specific types include protein-energy undernutrition, imbalanced nutritional status, and vitamin deficiency diseases."}, {"sources": [3], "text": "Causes of malnutrition include an unbalanced diet, medical issues like cancer or eating disorders, and problems with swallowing or digestion."}, {"sources": [3], "text": "Other contributing factors include certain medicines that affect taste and smell, or an inability to access or prepare food due to chronic illness or low income."}, {"sources": [1, 3], "text": "Although it can affect anyone, children, older adults, and people with chronic health problems are at a higher risk."}, {"sources": [2, 3], "text": "Symptoms may include fatigue, weakness, dizziness, unintentional weight loss, frequent infections, and dry skin or brittle hair."}]}

{"covered": true, "see_a_professional": false, "sentences": [{"sources": [1], "text": "As people age, their bodies and lives change, which can make it harder to eat healthy."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "Changes in home life, such as living alone or having trouble getting around, can impact nutrition."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "Health issues can make it more difficult for older adults to cook or feed themselves."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "Medicines can change how food tastes, cause dry mouth, or reduce appetite."}, {"sources": [4], "text": "Older adults are specifically identified as a group at higher risk for developing malnutrition."}, {"sources": [4], "text": "Chronic illness, mobility issues, or low income can prevent older adults from getting or cooking food."}, {"sources": [3], "text": "Older adults are at higher risk for vitamin D deficiency because their skin produces less vitamin D from sunlight."}, {"sources": [3], "text": "The kidneys of older adults are less able to convert vitamin D to its active form."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "While older adults may need fewer calories, they still require enough nutrients to stay healthy."}]}

{"covered": true, "see_a_professional": false, "sentences": [{"sources": [1], "text": "Nutritional support is a therapy for people who cannot get enough nourishment by eating or drinking."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "You may need this support if you cannot swallow, have problems with your appetite, are severely malnourished, or cannot absorb nutrients through your digestive system."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "The therapy is delivered through a needle or catheter placed in a vein or via a feeding tube that goes into the stomach."}, {"sources": [3], "text": "For short bowel syndrome, the main treatment is nutrition support, which may depend on the stage and severity of the condition."}, {"sources": [3], "text": "During the acute stage of short bowel syndrome, doctors may recommend parenteral nutrition through an IV or enteral nutrition through a tube."}, {"sources": [3], "text": "Your doctor may refer you to a registered dietitian to help ensure you get enough nutrients."}]}

{"covered": true, "see_a_professional": false, "sentences": [{"sources": [3], "text": "Short bowel syndrome is a condition where the small intestine cannot absorb enough water, vitamins, minerals, protein, fat, and calories from food and drinks."}, {"sources": [3], "text": "This inability to absorb nutrients is known as malabsorption."}, {"sources": [3], "text": "Malabsorption can lead to dehydration, low levels of specific vitamins and minerals, and general malnutrition."}, {"sources": [3], "text": "In infants and children, this condition can also cause problems with growth and development."}, {"sources": [5], "text": "The primary treatment for this condition is nutrition support, which varies based on the stage and severity of the syndrome."}, {"sources": [5], "text": "During the acute stage, doctors may recommend parenteral nutrition, which delivers nutrients through an IV, or enteral nutrition, which uses a tube to deliver liquid food."}, {"sources": [2], "text": "If the intestines stop adapting and still cannot absorb enough nutrients, the condition is called chronic intestinal failure."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "Treatment goals include ensuring adequate nutrient intake, preventing complications, and reducing the need for long-term intravenous nutrition."}, {"sources": [5], "text": "Doctors may refer patients to a registered dietitian to help ensure they receive sufficient nutrients."}]}

{"covered": true, "see_a_professional": false, "sentences": [{"sources": [1, 2], "text": "Body mass index (BMI) is a measurement that uses a person's weight and height to estimate whether they have a healthy weight, are overweight, or have obesity."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "For adults ages 20 and older, specific BMI ranges are used to define categories of overweight and obesity."}, {"sources": [3], "text": "An adult with a BMI of 30 or more is considered to have obesity."}, {"sources": [3], "text": "Severe obesity is defined as having a BMI of 40 or higher."}, {"sources": [2, 4], "text": "BMI does not directly measure the amount of body fat, so it may not be the best way to assess health risks for everyone."}, {"sources": [2, 4], "text": "For example, very muscular individuals may have a high BMI without having excess body fat."}, {"sources": [2, 4], "text": "Older adults may have a normal BMI but still face increased health risks due to age-related changes in body composition, such as losing muscle and gaining fat."}, {"sources": [2, 4], "text": "People with Asian ancestry may store extra fat around their waist, increasing health risks even if their BMI is not high."}, {"sources": [4], "text": "Health care providers may also check waist size, as carrying extra fat around the abdomen increases the risk for weight-related health problems."}]}

{"covered": true, "see_a_professional": false, "sentences": [{"sources": [5], "text": "Obesity can increase the risk of type 2 diabetes, heart disease, high blood pressure, stroke, metabolic syndrome, osteoarthritis, sleep apnea, and some cancers."}, {"sources": [5], "text": "Having a larger body size puts extra pressure on joints and makes the heart work harder."}, {"sources": [4], "text": "During pregnancy, obesity raises the risk of gestational diabetes, preeclampsia, and the need for a caesarean delivery."}, {"sources": [4], "text": "Babies born to mothers with obesity may be larger than expected and face higher risks of developing chronic diseases like type 2 diabetes and heart disease as adults."}, {"sources": [2], "text": "Obesity is linked to infertility, lower sperm quality in men, and menstrual or ovulation problems in women."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "Obesity can affect mental health by increasing the risk of depression, low self-esteem, body image problems, and eating disorders."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "People with obesity may also face weight-related bias at school and work, which can harm their quality of life."}]}

{"covered": true, "see_a_professional": true, "sentences": [{"sources": [1], "text": "Treatment plans for obesity depend on your overall weight, other health conditions, and your willingness to participate in a weight-loss plan."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "A healthcare provider can help you set goals and may refer you to specialists in nutrition or weight loss for support."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "Possible treatments include dietary changes, exercise goals, counseling, support groups, and weight-loss medicines."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "Weight-loss surgery is an option for adults with severe obesity or serious obesity-related health problems who have not lost enough weight through other methods."}, {"sources": [2], "text": "Surgery may be considered for adults with a BMI of 40 or more, or a BMI of 35 or more with serious health problems like type 2 diabetes or heart disease."}, {"sources": [2], "text": "Surgery is also an option for adults with a BMI of 30 or more who have type 2 diabetes that is difficult to control with medical treatments and lifestyle changes."}, {"sources": [5], "text": "A healthy eating plan for weight loss involves reducing calorie intake and including vegetables, fruits, whole grains, and lean proteins."}, {"sources": [5], "text": "Adults should limit added sugars, saturated fat, and sodium as part of a healthy eating plan."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "A doctor or registered dietitian should advise you on the specific treatment plan that is right for you."}]}

{"covered": true, "see_a_professional": false, "sentences": [{"sources": [1, 2, 5], "text": "Adults with a body mass index of 40 or higher are generally considered good candidates for weight-loss surgery."}, {"sources": [1, 2, 5], "text": "Those with a BMI of 35 or higher who have serious obesity-related health problems, such as type 2 diabetes, heart disease, or sleep apnea, may also be candidates."}, {"sources": [1, 2], "text": "Individuals with a BMI of 30 to 35 who have type 2 diabetes that is difficult to control with medications and lifestyle changes might be considered for surgery."}, {"sources": [1, 2], "text": "Candidates typically have not been able to lose weight or keep it off using nonsurgical methods like diet, exercise, or medication."}, {"sources": [2], "text": "Potential candidates must be willing to commit to lifelong healthy eating, physical activity, medical follow-up, and taking extra vitamins and minerals."}, {"sources": [3], "text": "Teens with severe obesity and a BMI of 40, or a BMI of 35 or higher with serious health problems, may also be evaluated for surgery by a specialized team."}, {"sources": [2], "text": "It is important to understand the risks, benefits, and costs of the operation before making a decision."}]}

{"covered": true, "see_a_professional": false, "sentences": [{"sources": [1], "text": "After weight-loss surgery, your body may not absorb enough nutrients, especially if you do not take prescribed vitamins and minerals."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "Not getting enough nutrients can cause health problems such as anemia and osteoporosis."}, {"sources": [4], "text": "Gastric bypass surgery carries a higher chance of vitamin and iron shortage compared to gastric band or gastric sleeve procedures."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "Gallstones can also occur after the rapid weight loss that follows the surgery."}, {"sources": [3], "text": "The procedure works by bypassing parts of the stomach and small intestine, which reduces the amount of calories and nutrients your body absorbs."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "Some health care professionals prescribe medicine for about six months after surgery to help prevent gallstones."}, {"sources": [4], "text": "Because of the altered anatomy, patients are at increased risk for specific nutrient deficiencies that require ongoing monitoring."}]}

{"covered": true, "see_a_professional": false, "sentences": [{"sources": [2, 4], "text": "Metabolic syndrome is a group of conditions that increase your risk for heart disease, diabetes, and stroke."}, {"sources": [2, 4], "text": "To be diagnosed with metabolic syndrome, you must have at least three of the following conditions: large waist size, high triglycerides, high blood pressure, high fasting blood glucose, or low HDL cholesterol."}, {"sources": [4], "text": "A large waistline, also known as abdominal obesity, is a significant risk factor because fat around the stomach poses a greater risk to heart health than fat in other areas."}, {"sources": [4], "text": "High triglycerides are a type of fat found in the blood, while low HDL cholesterol means you have less of the \"good\" cholesterol that helps remove cholesterol from arteries."}, {"sources": [4], "text": "High blood pressure can damage the heart over time, and high fasting blood sugar may be an early sign of diabetes."}, {"sources": [4], "text": "The more of these risk factors you have, the higher your overall risk for heart disease, diabetes, and stroke."}, {"sources": [2, 4], "text": "Metabolic syndrome is closely linked to overweight, obesity, and a lack of physical activity."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "People with metabolic syndrome often also experience excessive blood clotting and inflammation throughout the body."}]}

{"covered": true, "see_a_professional": true, "sentences": [{"sources": [2], "text": "The main goals of treating metabolic syndrome are to lower your risk of heart disease and to prevent type 2 diabetes if it hasn't already developed."}, {"sources": [2, 3], "text": "Heart-healthy lifestyle changes are the first line of treatment for metabolic syndrome."}, {"sources": [3], "text": "A heart-healthy eating plan limits saturated and trans fats while encouraging fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and lean meats."}, {"sources": [3], "text": "Other important lifestyle changes include aiming for a healthy weight, managing stress, getting regular physical activity, and quitting smoking."}, {"sources": [2], "text": "You may need to see a dietitian and a physical therapist to help find a diet and exercise plan that works for you."}, {"sources": [1, 2], "text": "If healthy lifestyle changes do not work, you may need medicines or weight loss surgery."}, {"sources": [1], "text": "Medicines may be needed to lower cholesterol or blood pressure."}, {"sources": [2], "text": "You may also need treatment for other health conditions that caused your metabolic syndrome or can make it worse."}, {"sources": [], "text": "A doctor or registered dietitian should advise you on specific treatment options."}]}
